[Root.GetCouncillorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].

The Jade Viceroy, who keeps the western marches of the Celestial Empire in the name of the Dragon Emperor, wishes to know the lords beyond the Great Bastion better. My [From.Liege.GetMasterMistress] has sent me west on the long road, and it would honour me to visit your court and [From.GetCGMission].

I await your answer with the patience of jade.

[Root.GetCouncillorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].

As a loyal tributary of the Dragon Throne, you will understand that the Jade Viceroy must look after the Emperor's western children. My [From.Liege.GetMasterMistress] has sent me to your demesne to see that the bonds between our lands stay strong. I shall visit your court and [From.GetCGMission].

Prepare a fitting welcome.
The servants of the [From.Liege.GetTitle] are always welcome here.
I have no time to entertain guests from the far East.
The [From.GetJobTitle] of §Y[From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]§!, §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§!, will visit your court.\n
Your refusal is a great insult to §Y[From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]§! and [From.Liege.GetHerHis] [From.GetJobTitle] §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§!.\n

After a tour of [Root.Capital.GetName] and a fortnight at my court, [From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName] takes [From.GetHerHis] leave. My own [corresponding_councilor.GetJobTitle], [corresponding_councilor.GetTitledFirstName], saw to every detail, from the order of the dishes to the number of bows at the gate, and not one thing went amiss. The [From.GetJobTitle] goes back east with [From.GetCGMissionOutcome] for the Jade Viceroy, and with kind words about my court.
Let the Viceroy hear of us.

When the welcoming feast is over, [From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName] and I walk the walls of [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName] to finish our talk under the moons. Then streaks of fire cross the sky, one after another, and the [From.GetJobTitle] goes grey in the face. 'The Dragons of Heaven are angry,' the translator mutters. Before dawn my guests are gone, back down the eastern road without a word of farewell.

When the welcoming feast is over, [From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName] and I walk the walls of [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName] to finish our talk under the moons. Streaks of fire cross the sky, and the old court astrologers would have wailed at the omen. We are both too old for that. The [From.GetJobTitle] laughs and says the Dragons of Heaven are only lighting our way home after too much rice wine.
Wait, come back! We were getting on so well!
§Y[From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName]§! leaves at once, sure that Heaven has cursed the visit.\n
Then let us raise one more cup to them.

[From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName] arrives tomorrow, and the preparations are well in hand. A translator who has walked the Ivory Road twice stands ready. Still, it would be a fine gesture to greet my guest in the tongue of Grand Cathay, with all its rising and falling tones, each of which seems to change the meaning entirely...
I shall spend ALL NIGHT on the most elegant phrases!
An hour or two on a simple greeting should do.
How fortunate that I already speak the tongue.
Better not. The translator knows the tones, I do not.
a long night of study. Your greeting tomorrow will be flawless.
you falling asleep over your study, and being late to the audience.
you making a good attempt at the greeting.
you making a clumsy attempt at the greeting.
You greet your guest flawlessly in the tongue of Grand Cathay.\n
You leave the talking to the translator. §Y[cathayan_guest.GetTitledName]§! is content and goes home in good time.\n

I had the translator teach me not only the sounds, but the grammar and the meaning behind each word, and why the word for 'four' must never be said at a feast. It took the whole night and most of the candles. But the look on [FromFrom.GetJobTitle] [FromFrom.GetDynName]'s [FromFrom.GetFaceDescription] face as I greet [FromFrom.GetHerHim] in flawless Cathayan was worth every hour.
There is more power in words than most [Root.GetMenWomen] know.
Your guest is delighted, and §Y[cathayan_guest.GetTitledName]§! goes home full of praise. §Y[FromFrom.Liege.GetTitle] [FromFrom.Liege.GetDynName]§! will hear of your courtesy.\n

'My [Root.GetLordLady], please wake up!' I sit up with a start, a page of brush strokes stuck to my cheek. The library. 'Your guests are waiting! Forgive me, my [Root.GetLordLady], we searched the whole [Root.Capital.Capital.GetHolding] for you!' I have not even greeted the Viceroy's envoy, and the visit is already a disaster.
Curse these Cathayans and their dawn audiences!
§Y[cathayan_guest.GetTitledName]§! goes home offended. §Y[FromFrom.Liege.GetTitle] [FromFrom.Liege.GetDynName]§! will hear of your manners.\n

I spent an hour with the greeting the translator wrote out for me, and [FromFrom.GetSheHe] coached me again while I dressed. I have no idea what the long phrases mean, but they come out smoothly enough as I bow to [FromFrom.GetJobTitle] [FromFrom.GetDynName], who bows lower still.
That went well, I think!
§Y[FromFrom.GetJobTitle] [FromFrom.GetDynName]§! values the effort, and goes home to §Y[FromFrom.Liege.GetTitle] [FromFrom.Liege.GetDynName]§! with a good report.\n

I spent an hour with the greeting the translator wrote out for me. But as I stood before [FromFrom.GetJobTitle] [FromFrom.GetDynName] this morning, every other word fled my mind, and the ones that stayed came out in the wrong tones. Judging by the translator's face, I may have called my guest's mother a river turtle.
I have never been so ashamed!
You made a fool of yourself, and §Y[FromFrom.GetJobTitle] [FromFrom.GetDynName]§! goes home offended.\n

For [From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName]'s arrival I had a merchant of the Ivory Road find me a robe of the finest Cathayan silk, with all the proper ornaments. Yet when I came out to greet my guest, [From.GetSheHe] went rigid. Later the translator explained, very quietly, that the five-clawed dragon on my sleeves may be worn by no one but the family of the Dragon Emperor himself.
Guards! Bring me that merchant, and my money!
Well, at least I looked magnificent.
§Y[From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName]§! goes home offended. [From.GetHerHisCap] [From.Liege.GetMasterMistress], §Y[From.Liege.GetTitle] [From.Liege.GetDynName]§!, will surely hear of it.\n

Walking in the gardens with [From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName], I remark on the clear sky. The translator repeats my words, and after a long silence [From.GetDynName] answers with great warmth. It seems [From.GetSheHe] took my small talk for an elegant saying about the Dragon Emperor, the Son of Heaven, under whose rule no cloud may darken the sky.

Walking in the gardens with [From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName], I remark on the clear sky, and quote an old verse about the sun on the Jade Sea. My guest finishes it from memory, and we spend the afternoon trading verses like scholars at the Imperial examinations.
Who knew the weather could be so fruitful?
§Y[From.GetJobTitle] [From.GetDynName]§! goes home, sure that you praised the §Y[From.Offmap.Ruler.GetMediumCathayanEmperorName]§!. Word of your wisdom will reach the Dragon Throne.\n

[From.GetTitledName], the [From.GetJobTitle] sent by [offmap_cathay.Governor.GetTitledFirstName], has died at my court. It is a sad loss, and it leaves me with the delicate task of telling the Jade Viceroy that [From.GetHerHis] envoy will not be coming home.

[From.GetTitledName], the [From.GetJobTitle] sent by [offmap_cathay.Governor.GetTitledFirstName], is in a cell. However it came to this, the visit is over, and I have no idea how to word the letter to the Jade Viceroy.

[From.GetTitledName], the [From.GetJobTitle] sent by [offmap_cathay.Governor.GetTitledFirstName], has vanished without a trace. The visit is over, and I have no idea how to word the letter to the Jade Viceroy.
Have my scribes write to the [offmap_cathay.Governor.GetTitle], with a gift.
The [offmap_cathay.Governor.GetTitle] will find out sooner or later.
teach your subjects the harmony of the Celestial Dragon
debate the nature of the gods with your [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nIt has come to the attention of the [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetShortCathayanEmperorName] that the merchants of your lands cheat the caravans of the Celestial Empire on the long roads east. They water the wine, shave the silver and weigh jade with a thumb on the scale. The Jade Viceroy is certain that you will put an end to this at once, before the Emperor's patience, which is long but not endless, runs out.
Curb the privileges of the great trade guilds.
[target_spymaster.GetFirstName] will find the worst of the cheats.
How our merchants trade is no business of the crown.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has curbed the merchants of my cities, citing their misdeeds with the caravans of Cathay. Many in [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] say the guilds of my lands are no business of [From.GetTitledFirstName], let alone of some Viceroy beyond the mountains. It might anger the [From.GetTitle], but I could take a public stand.
I will speak out against this misuse of power!
Better to stay in [From.GetFirstName]'s good graces.

Your vassal, [From.GetTitledFirstName], was not pleased that you curbed the merchants of [From.GetHerHis] cities to please the Jade Viceroy. [From.GetSheHeCap] has declared in public that you overstepped your rights in a matter that is [From.GetHerHis] own concern.
[From.GetHerHisCap] merchants had to be kept in line!

Last night [cathayan_courtier.GetBestName] and I talked until dawn about [cathayan_courtier.GetRootMatchingPersonalityStreak]. I must have made a fine impression, for [cathayan_courtier.GetSheHe] says [cathayan_courtier.GetSheHe] will write home to the Celestial Court in praise of the hospitality of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName].
A pleasant evening.
Everyone should hear of this.

[cathayan_courtier.GetBestName] has been growing ever more short with me these last weeks, and today something careless slipped from my tongue. [cathayan_courtier.GetSheHeCap] stormed off, crying that the Dragon Emperor himself would hear of this insult.
This may sour our dealings with [offmap_cathay.GetShortName].
Guards, arrest that [cathayan_courtier.GetManWoman]!

My [adventurous_spirit.GetRootRelation] [adventurous_spirit.GetFirstName] kneels before me, eyes shining. 'My [Root.GetLordLady], let me go east! The Jade Viceroy holds court at Taharq, at the very edge of the Celestial Empire. I would carry your name there, learn their ways and bring home the favour of the [the_protector_general.Offmap.Ruler.GetShortCathayanEmperorName]. Please. Let a humble servant win you friends beyond the mountains.'
A splendid idea! Go, with my blessing.
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! beams like the sun and runs off to pack.\n
[back_up_target_1.GetTitledFirstName] is better suited to the journey.
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! looks crestfallen as §Y[back_up_target_1.GetTitledFirstName]§! is sent in [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] place.\n
Forgive me, but [back_up_target_2.GetTitledFirstName] would make a better impression.
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! looks crestfallen as §Y[back_up_target_2.GetTitledFirstName]§! is sent in [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] place.\n
Absolutely not. You are needed here, [adventurous_spirit.GetFirstName].
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! looks crestfallen.\n

I wake one morning before my guards come to rouse me. There is excited chatter in the hall, and when I open the [Root.GetChamberOpening] the [Root.GetCapitalHolding] is a bustle of servants. '[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName] is back from the court of the Jade Viceroy!' they whisper. 'With carts! And a letter sealed in jade!'
And [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] comes bearing gifts? Excellent!
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! proudly brings home the favour of the [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName].\n

'The [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName] is a marvel, my [Root.GetLordLady],' says [adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName], as I turn a square-holed copper coin over in my hand. [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHeCap] came home this morning with a chest of trinkets and more tales than a minstrel: of jade warriors that never sleep, of sky lanterns over the river, and of [adventurous_spirit.GetCathayanConvoTopic]. The whole [Root.GetCapitalHolding] wants to hear everything.
Bear with us, [adventurous_spirit.GetFirstName], while my scribes write it all down!
The journey of §Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! to the [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName] was a success!\n

[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName] reached [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName] late last night, worn out by the road. At today's audience [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] mostly looks glad to be home, and I begin to wonder what impression [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] made out east. Then [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] hands me a letter of greeting, sealed by the Jade Viceroy [the_protector_general.GetHerselfHimself].
Not a complete failure, then.

[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledName] is back from [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] travels. When my council asks what [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] made of the [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName], [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] sighs heavily and launches into a tirade about [adventurous_spirit.GetNegativeCathayanConvoTopic].
This is not what I had hoped for...
You lose a little grace.\n

[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledName] has finally come home from the [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName]. Asked about [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] adventures, [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] only mutters about [adventurous_spirit.GetNegativeCathayanConvoTopic]. A letter from Taharq that arrived a week earlier tells the rest, in very polite and very cold words.
I should have sent someone else.
You lose some grace.\n

On the eve of [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] return from the [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName], [adventurous_spirit.GetFirstName] and I talk at length about [adventurous_spirit.GetCathayanConvoTopic].\n'There is also someone I would like you to meet,' [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] says, smiling, as a stranger in Cathayan silks bows low at the door.
How lovely! Welcome to the [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName]!
A [new_found_lover.GetManWoman] named §Y[new_found_lover.GetTitledName]§! joins your court.\n
You brought a stranger into our [Root.GetCapitalHolding]?
The stranger goes home to Cathay. §Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will not forgive you.\n

Something has changed in [adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]. As we talk of [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] travels to the [the_protector_general.Offmap.GetFullName], [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] speaks with a fire I have never seen about [adventurous_spirit.GetCathayanConvoTopic]. 'Oh, my [Root.GetLordLady],' [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] pleads. 'You must let me go back.'
If this is what you want...
What, you want to LIVE there?!
I am not sure I follow...
I... understand the wish to follow a dream.
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will leave your court forever.\n
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will leave your court forever, taking [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] spouse and young children.\n
Out of the question! You belong here in [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName].
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! is furious.\n
Oh, [adventurous_spirit.GetFirstName]. Surely you do not mean that?
§Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will get over it.\n
How can you ask me to send you away again, [adventurous_spirit.GetFirstName]?

This option is available because §Y[adventurous_spirit.GetTitledName]§! thinks so highly of you.

Your [adventurous_spirit.GetRootRelation] bows [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] head and promises to stay.

A letter comes from Taharq, sealed in green wax. The Jade Viceroy writes, in careful and courteous phrases, that [adventurous_spirit.GetTitledFirstName] has died at the Viceroy's court, far from home, and was buried with all the rites the Celestial Empire grants an honoured guest.
At least [the_protector_general.GetTitledFirstName] sends [the_protector_general.GetHerHis] condolences.
Perhaps [adventurous_spirit.GetSheHe] at least enjoyed [adventurous_spirit.GetHerHis] last days abroad.\n
how the Celestial Empire is so full of life, and there are people everywhere
how the realm is so wealthy, and every inch of the Celestial Empire seems to be used to house or feed its people

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] has decreed that a new city shall rise on the roads that link the Celestial Empire to the West, where caravans may rest and jade and silk change hands. The lord who founds it first will enjoy the Emperor's favour in trade, and [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetHerHis] personal notice. You are one of those the Jade Viceroy has named to the task.

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] wishes to know which of the lords of the West is the most worthy to trade with the Celestial Empire. In five years the Jade Viceroy will judge who among those named has won the greatest renown, and that lord will enjoy the Emperor's favour in trade, and [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetHerHis] personal notice.
Failure is not an option...
To win, be the first contestant to build a new §YCity§! holding in a province on the Ivory Road, the Old Silk Road, the Khyprian Road or the Spice Route, within five years.\n
To win, gain more §YPrestige§! than any other contestant over the next five years.\n

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] is most pleased with the city of [trade_competition_new_city.GetName], which you raised on the road east. The caravans already speak of its markets. To show [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetHerHis] appreciation, the Celestial Empire grants you its favour.

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] is most pleased with the city of [trade_competition_new_city.GetName], which [trade_competition_winner.GetTitledName] raised on the road east. Your own lack of zeal for trade with the Celestial Empire has also been noted.
To be noticed by the Dragon Emperor himself!
I must try harder next time.

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] is most displeased that not one of the lords named by the Jade Viceroy has raised so much as a market on the roads east in five years. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetHerHisCap] disappointment is great, and it will not soon be forgotten.
Alas! Woe to us all...
Pleasant rumours reach my court from the East: the Jade Viceroy is said to think me the most worthy of those competing for the Emperor's favour.
Rumours reach my court from the East: the Jade Viceroy is said to think [trade_competition_halftime_winner.GetTitledName] the most worthy of those competing for the Emperor's favour.
Of course I am.
Keep winning more renown than the other contestants to win.\n
I must work harder to deserve it...
Win more renown than the other contestants before the five years are up.\n

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] has heard much of the esteem you command among your peers, more than any other the Jade Viceroy named. The Celestial Empire is honoured to call you its friend.

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nThe [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetTitle] [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetFullName] has heard much of the esteem [trade_competition_winner.GetTitledName] commands among [trade_competition_winner.GetHerHis] peers. Your own renown, however, fell short.

A noble named [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName] came to court today, dusty from the long road west, and begged for asylum. [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetSheHeCap] says [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetHerHis] whole family fell from favour at the Celestial Court and was put to death by order of the Dragon Emperor, and that [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetSheHe] alone escaped over the Great Bastion. 'Great [Root.GetTitle], your mercy is known even in the East. Grant me refuge, and I will never forget it.'
Of course you may stay.
§Y[escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName]§! may stay at your court.\n
Is there, perhaps, a price on your head?
§Y[escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName]§! may stay, and you secretly write to the Jade Viceroy.\n
I dare not anger the Dragon.
You send §Y[escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName]§! away, so as not to anger the Dragon Emperor.\n

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetCathayanLetterBlessing].\n\nIt has come to the attention of the [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetShortCathayanEmperorName] that you shelter [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName], a traitor condemned by the Celestial Court. If the traitor is not handed over to the Jade Viceroy's guards at once, the Dragon will be most displeased.
Then I had better hand [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetHerHim] over.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! receives your reply.\n
I do not fear the Emperor!
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! receives your reply.\n

Despite [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName]'s fears, no envoy of the Dragon Emperor has come looking for [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetHerHim]. 'The time has come for me to go further west, where no one knows my name. I will never forget your kindness. Please, take this in thanks.'
I will treasure it always.
§Y[escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFirstName]§! leaves your court.\n

Soon after my letter reached Taharq, an envoy of the Jade Viceroy came with a dozen jade-armoured guards to take [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName] back east, with many thanks. 'You do not know what they will do to me!' [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFirstName] screamed as [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetSheHe] was dragged out to the waiting cart.
Surely it cannot be that bad?

An envoy of the Jade Viceroy came with a dozen jade-armoured guards, but [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName] had fled the night before. Someone must have warned [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetHerHim]. All the envoy said before leaving was: 'The Dragon will be... displeased.'
What a fool I look.

[escaped_cathayan_noble.GetFullName] was found dead in [escaped_cathayan_noble.GetHerHis] room this morning, strangled with a cord of the finest Cathayan silk. The killer was gone without a trace, but I have no doubt who sent them.
No one escapes the Dragon.

A nervous foreigner in travel-stained silks has come to court. [cathayan_refugee.GetSheHeCap] flinches whenever anyone comes near, yet will not be sent on [cathayan_refugee.GetHerHis] way. [cathayan_refugee.GetSheHeCap] was a trained [cathayan_refugee.GetCathayanProfession] of the Celestial Empire, [cathayan_refugee.GetSheHe] says, and can keep my ledgers as well as any scribe of the Jade Viceroy. [cathayan_refugee.GetCelestialRefugeeCause]\n\n"Only do not send me back east. I cannot go back", [cathayan_refugee.GetSheHe] says, jaw clenched.

My guards have dragged a Cathayan thief before me. "[cathayan_refugee.GetSheHeCap] claimed to have an audience with you, my [Root.GetLordLady]", they report.\n\n"Forgive the ruse", the [cathayan_refugee.GetManWoman] begs in a heavy accent. "I am a [cathayan_refugee.GetCathayanProfession]. I have raised walls on the Great Bastion and built rockets for the Imperial batteries. Any court in Cathay would fight to have me!" [cathayan_refugee.GetCelestialRefugeeCause] "Take pity on me, [Root.GetMasterMistress]."

A suspected spy tried to slip into [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName] tonight, and was caught only because the guards saw the glint of lamellar under [cathayan_refugee.GetHerHis] cloak. Brought before me, the foreigner claims to be a [cathayan_refugee.GetCathayanProfession] of the [offmap_cathay.GetFullName]. [cathayan_refugee.GetCelestialRefugeeCause]\n\nThe face is worn to the bone, and the armour is caked not only with the dust of the long road, but with old, dark blood.

A Cathayan healer has taken shelter in a village outside [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName], treating the sick for bread and a roof, and curing more than my own physicians do. My courier took the [cathayan_refugee.GetManWoman] for a beggar at first. [cathayan_refugee.GetCelestialRefugeeCause]\n\n"It would explain the rags, my [Root.GetLordLady]. And the needles, and the jars of things I would rather not name."
You may stay. The [offmap_cathay.GetFullName] is no place for anyone right now.
That is no thief, you fools. [cathayan_refugee.GetSheHeCap] is a refugee!
I can use a veteran like you.
Why was I not told sooner? Bring [cathayan_refugee.GetHerHim] to court!
The Cathayan [cathayan_refugee.GetManWoman] joins your court.
Surely this [cathayan_refugee.GetManWoman] can find shelter elsewhere.
A thief with a good story is still a thief. Out.
I am sorry, but we can hardly feed our own.
Leave the healer to the villagers.
You turn the [cathayan_refugee.GetManWoman] away. Alone and far from home, [cathayan_refugee.GetSheHe] will not last long.
The hordes of the Northern Wastes are at the Great Bastion, and the lands behind the wall are emptying.
Hobgoblin hordes are riding over the eastern steppe into Cathay, burning as they come.
The Ogre tribes are raiding down from the Mountains of Mourn, and whole towns have been eaten.
The ratmen have boiled up from under the cities of Cathay, and nowhere is safe from the tunnels.
The Celestial Empire has turned on itself, and the losing side's servants flee for their lives.
Famine stalks the rice lands of Cathay, and the granaries are empty.
A plague is sweeping through Cathay, and the dead lie unburied in the streets.
Invaders are pouring into Cathay, and its people are fleeing.

My messengers tell of a traveller lodging in [tavern_location.GetName], where the caravans from the East rest. [traveling_teacher.GetSheHeCap] is a scholar of the Celestial Court by the name of [traveling_teacher.GetFullName], who has walked the long road from Grand Cathay with nothing but a satchel of scrolls. [traveling_teacher.GetSheHeCap] asks for an audience, and offers to teach one of my children what the sages of the East know.
Intriguing. Bring [traveling_teacher.GetHerHim] to court!
I have no time for wandering sages.
Bring [traveling_teacher.GetHerHim] to a quiet dinner. Just the two of us.
You invite the travelling scholar to your court.
You turn the travelling scholar away.
You invite the scholar to a private, secluded dinner.

The scholar bows low before me. "I greet the [Root.GetCathayanComplimentAdjective] [Root.GetFirstName] of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName]! I am [traveling_teacher.GetFullName], and I come with an offer. For a modest fee I will teach your [child_to_be_taught.GetDaughterSon] [child_to_be_taught.GetFirstName] one of my arts. I have studied the classics of the Celestial Court, the verses of the Jade Poets and the healing of the body, and the Celestial Dragon frowns on wisdom kept to oneself."
Can you teach [child_to_be_taught.GetHerHim] to read faster?
Teach [child_to_be_taught.GetHerHim] the classics of the Celestial Court!
Surgery and poetry sound useful.
My [child_to_be_taught.GetDaughterSon] is dull and listless. Can you wake [child_to_be_taught.GetHerHis] curiosity?
You ask an outrageous sum. Begone!

A merchant in fine eastern silks has asked for an audience. The [radhanite_merchant.GetManWoman] introduces [radhanite_merchant.GetHerselfHimself] as [radhanite_merchant.GetFullName], a factor of the caravan houses that carry jade, silk and gunpowder along the Ivory Road. "My masters wish to open a trade office in [radhanite_location.GetName], where the caravans pass, but the road has been costly this year. If you would sponsor us, the houses of the East do not forget their friends."
More trade is good for everyone. I shall sponsor you.
Let us discuss my patronage over... dinner.
A shabby office will not do. You shall govern [radhanite_location_barony.GetName]!
I am sorry, but I have no gold to spare.
The caravan houses open a modest trade office.
You give the caravan houses the city of [radhanite_location_barony.GetName]. Its burgher will not forgive you, but the Jade Viceroy will hear of your generosity.
You turn the caravan factor away.

A factor of the caravan houses has called, all smiles and bows, to remind me of the gold I borrowed from them. There is no hurry, the factor assures me, none at all. Yet I cannot help noticing that fewer caravans have stopped in my markets of late, and that those that do ask higher prices.
Pay them and be done with it.
They will get their gold when I have it to spare.
Borrow from the Caravan Houses
Borrow 200 gold from the Cathayan caravan houses that trade along the roads through my lands. They will expect 250 back, in time.
Repay the Caravan Houses
Pay the caravan houses the 250 gold I owe them.
Owes the Caravan Houses
This character owes gold to the Cathayan caravan houses of the Ivory Road, and the priests frown on debts to foreigners.
Caravan Office
A Cathayan caravan house keeps an office here, and the caravans of the Ivory Road stop to trade.
Caravan House Seat
A Cathayan caravan house governs a city here, and caravans from the East pass by almost every day.

The road to Wei-Jin, where the Celestial Throne stands empty while the Dragon Emperor and the Moon Empress are away on their long quest and their son Yuan Bo, the Jade Dragon, keeps the court, will take months, perhaps years. It is one of the most dangerous roads in the world: through the burning Dark Lands, over the Mountains of Mourn where the Ogres take their tithe, and across the Warpstone Desert, where the dust itself is poison. Those who come back are rich men. Most do not come back. I take leave of my near and dear and give the order to load the wagons.
To Grand Cathay!

Our caravan has sat by the roadside all day while the sky empties itself over us. The drumming of the rain on the canvas has carried my thoughts back to my late [target_relative.GetRootRelation], [target_relative.GetFirstName].
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] died far too young.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] kept the faith better than any of us.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] was always so clever.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] always saw what others could not.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] was the bravest soul I have known.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] charmed everyone with that smile.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] could always tell right from wrong.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] was always kind to me.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] was... not an easy person.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] was the wisest person I have known.
[target_relative.GetSheHeCap] was a good soul.
You burn incense to their memory and step out to let the rain wash away your tears.
I cannot dwell in the past. The road goes on.

A rider has caught up with the caravan bearing a letter under the seal of [target_host.GetBestName]. [target_host.GetFirstName] has heard of my journey east and invites my company to rest a while in the warmth of [target_host.GetHerHis] [target_host.GetCapitalHolding] at [target_host.Capital.Capital.GetName].
An old rival opens the door to me? An opportunity to get even.
You use your rival's hospitality to set up a risky poisoning.
A warm bed and a hot meal are most welcome.
Is my old rival ready to bury the hatchet?
You accept the invitation to the court of [target_host.GetTitledFirstName].
My tent will do.
A warm hearth and good meals have put new life in the whole company, but after some days of [target_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s hospitality it is time to take the road to Grand Cathay again.
These have been delightful days. I never imagined we had so much in common. It is with regret that I bid [target_host.GetTitledFirstName] farewell and turn my face east again.

A splendid meal is laid before us, and [target_host.GetTitledFirstName] raises [target_host.GetHerHis] cup in a toast to my health. Thirsty from the road, I take a long draught, and only then see [target_host.GetFirstName] turn [target_host.GetHerHis] own cup over and pour it on the floor, laughing like a madman.
Thank you for being an excellent host.
Let us keep in touch.
Thank you, but we must be on our way.
You... you...!
The room starts spinning and you black out.
I wake in a ditch beside the road. In my pocket is a letter in a firm hand: 'This is your last warning. Stay out of my lands.'
Everything hurts.
You roll over and empty your bowels into the ditch.
Fatal Hospitality

'Trust is such a delicate thing', I tell my horse as we gallop into the dark, while screams and clattering plates and panic fill the hall behind us. Some of my servants had to pay with their lives to make the charade believable, but that is a price worth paying.

Just as I am about to slip out into the night, the captain of the guard stops me. Sweat beads on my temples. Any moment now.\nThen comes the bellow of [target_host.GetTitledFirstName] as the poison takes hold. For a heartbeat I see shock on the captain's face as someone cries that the [target_host.GetTitle] is dead. Then his eyes settle on me. Without a word, the burly man raises his sword.

During the dinner, [target_host.GetTitledFirstName] announces a present for me. Moments later a man with an arrow in his back is dragged into the hall, and with dread I recognise the servant I sent to poison [target_host.GetFirstName]. Pointing at me, [target_host.GetFirstName] shouts: 'Treachery! Kill them all!' From every corner, guards with drawn blades close in on my company.
[target_host.GetSheHeCap] should have known better than to trust me.
Now we are even!
There is no escape!

'Halt!' rasps a voice as we near a bridge. Wolf riders slink out of the rocks on either side. 'I am [other_ruler.GetTitledName], and this bridge belongs to the Khan's boys now. You, my fine [Root.GetLordLady], will pay the toll.' The hobgoblin's yellow grin tells me the toll could be anything he likes.
Pay the creature and let us be on our way.
You and your company are let through.
We will have none of that.
You hurl a spear through the hobgoblin before the grin leaves his face.
I do not pay greenskins. Guards, my sword!

'Ahh, there you are!' booms a voice, and a huge ogre steps out of the trees beside our camp with a dozen of his kin, all gut-plates and cleavers. 'I am [other_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]. We were paid half to guard a lord's caravan to [Root.GetRandomCathayanRegion], and we want the other half.' [other_ruler.GetSheHeCap] signals his ogres to sit down at our fire and eat our supper.
Ah, yes... there has been a change of plans. You are hired.
You never hired these ogres, but your caravan could use the protection, as long as you keep them fed.
I think you have me confused with someone else.
You explain the mistake. The ogres grumble, finish your supper and lumber off.

A band of soldiers in tattered Cathayan lamellar blocks the road. 'Please, we have not eaten in weeks', says a gaunt [other_ruler.GetManWoman] at their head, then tries to stand straighter. 'I am [other_ruler.GetTitledName]. You will let my soldiers eat with your people tonight!' The threat sounds empty from someone who can barely stay upright.
No need for threats. We have food enough for all.
[other_ruler.GetTitledName] and [other_ruler.GetHerHis] soldiers are grateful for your kindness.
Cathay has done nothing for you. Serve me instead!
[other_ruler.GetTitledName] leaves the deserters and joins your court.
We cannot afford pity for strangers.
The deserters stumble out of your way.

As the days drag on, I find myself thinking of [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName] and what may be happening at home. How is [person_missed.GetTitledFirstName] faring without me? When will I see [person_missed.GetHerHim] again, when the road to Grand Cathay never seems to end?
Halt! I must send a letter to my dear [person_missed.GetFirstName].
Halt! I must write to my friend.
Halt! I must send a letter to my [person_missed.GetHusbandWife].
Halt! I must send a letter to my [person_missed.GetFatherMother].
Halt! My [person_missed.GetSonDaughter] needs a letter from me.
No. My company needs me riding with them.
A Letter from the Road

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent me a letter. The road is long, it seems, and [From.GetSheHe] misses me terribly. 'You always have such interesting things to say, like when we spoke about [From.GetRootMatchingPersonalityStreak], remember?'
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent me a letter. 'The road is long', [From.GetSheHe] writes, 'and I find myself missing you terribly. I hope we can spend more time together when I am home.'
Oh... I do remember that!
I hope we will.

A smooth-faced [cathayan_trader.Culture.GetName] pedlar has ridden up beside our caravan. After a good deal of bowing, [cathayan_trader.GetSheHe] beckons me to [cathayan_trader.GetHerHis] horse, where something is wrapped in silk behind the saddle. 'The name is [cathayan_trader.GetBestName], my good [Root.GetLordLady]! Might this interest you?'
That looks [cathayan_artifact.GetArtifactDescriptor]. I will take it off your hands!
[cathayan_artifact.GetName] goes to your treasury.
You are quite the charmer. I could use someone like you.
The [cathayan_trader.GetManWoman] looks you up and down, then shrugs.\n[cathayan_trader.GetTitledName] joins your court.
Guards. I am suddenly in the mood for a gift.
Your guards cut the pedlar down and take the goods.
Flattery gets you nowhere, pedlar.
You have better things to do.

At last our company has come down out of the hills into the [offmap_cathay.GetFullName], past the iron foundries of Shang-Yang, the city of Zhao Ming the Iron Dragon. Jade-roofed towns line the Imperial road to Wei-Jin, sky lanterns drift over the rice terraces at dusk, and everywhere the banners of the Celestial Dragon snap in the wind. There is so much to see before the Jade Dragon receives me.
Let us walk, lest I forget why I came.
You take the Imperial road to the Celestial Palace at Wei-Jin.

Walking in a garden of Wei-Jin, I come upon a knot of courtiers bent over a square board, placing small black and white stones with great care. One move seems to take an age. This, my guide whispers, is the game of stones, and the Dragon Emperor himself is said to have taught it to the first scholars.
Let me show you how it is done.
How does one play this?
I will just enjoy the garden.

The rite is just beginning as I step into a temple of the Celestial Dragons. Incense hangs thick under the painted beams, and before a great jade dragon the priests chant of Yin and Yang and the harmony that keeps Grand Cathay whole.
Study their rite from a distance.
Join in the ceremony.
Loudly denounce these false gods.
Study the script on the temple walls.

A few days in Wei-Jin, and a group of ministers in silk robes calls upon me, offering to read with me from the Annals of the Jade Sages. They are sure that I, as a [Root.Religion.GetName], will find the chapters on the harmony of Yin and Yang most enlightening.
Of course! Tell me everything.
The ministers are delighted by your eagerness.
In fact, my lords, I know the Annals well.
The ministers are impressed by your learning.
Nonsense. I would rather see the palace.
The ministers make sure you are escorted through the public halls, and nowhere else.

My guards and I make our way through a crowded market of Wei-Jin. There are meats and spices I have never seen, porcelain, silks, jade and fireworks, and everywhere soldiers, scribes and envoys from far courts haggling with the stallholders. These traders want for nothing.
Mmm, what is that smell?
You eagerly try the local dishes.
I am here to trade. You there, let us talk business.
Your patronage of a trader lets you bring home a Cathayan treasure.
Guards... keep that trader busy.
You steal from a trader and bring home a Cathayan treasure.
I have seen enough for one day.

'The Celestial Court has watched your journey', the Chief Minister says. 'The Jade Dragon is, however, much occupied, and thinks it fitting that you bow here instead.' He gestures at a painting of the Dragon Emperor, absent these many years, on the wall of a side chamber. The throne room stays closed to me.

'The Celestial Court has watched your journey', the Chief Minister says. 'You may enter the throne room to show your submission. Be quick about it.' Beyond the doors the Celestial Throne stands empty, as it has since the Dragon Emperor left on his quest. Beside it, in the shape of a slender man robed in green, Yuan Bo the Jade Dragon watches me without a word, his gaze somewhere far above my head.

The Chief Minister opens the doors of the throne room and nods for me to enter. I bow before the empty Celestial Throne until my forehead touches the jade floor, three times and nine times, and then Yuan Bo the Jade Dragon, who keeps his father's court, comes down from the dais himself, reaches down and touches my brow. Warmth like a summer sun runs through me. 'Our father would have been pleased', he says.
Bow before the painting of the Emperor.
I will not be humiliated! Storm out of the room.
Kowtow quickly before the empty throne.
I am honoured beyond words.
War has broken out, and I cannot go on to the [offmap_cathay.GetFullName]. The caravan must turn for home.
The [offmap_cathay.GetFullName] has closed its gates and is driving all foreigners out. I cannot go on, and the caravan must turn for home.
I cannot go on to the [offmap_cathay.GetFullName]. The caravan must turn for home.
Another time, perhaps.

Before I leave, the old caravan masters of the city come to my hall. They have all walked the road east, and they are missing fingers, eyes and friends. 'No one crosses the Warpstone Desert without wards', the oldest says, 'the green dust gets into the blood. The Ogres of the Mountains of Mourn take their tithe from every caravan, in gold or in meat, and it is cheaper to pay ahead. And the Dark Lands... nothing helps in the Dark Lands but luck.' A merchant of Cathay, sitting apart, offers another way: passage on a junk of the Sea Dragon's fleet, months at sea round the Southlands to Fu-Chow.
Buy the wards and pay the tithe ahead.
Wards of a wizard and a priest will protect the caravan in the Warpstone Desert, and an Ogre escort will meet it in the Mountains of Mourn.
Buy the wards.
Wards will protect the caravan in the Warpstone Desert.
Pay the Ogres' tithe ahead.
An Ogre escort will meet the caravan in the Mountains of Mourn.
We will go by sea.
You avoid the dangers of the road, but the sea has its own: typhoons and, from far away, corsairs. Those who go by sea are not honoured as those who brave the road.
I trust in the gods and my sword.
The caravan sets out with nothing but faith against the dangers of the road.

The Warpstone Desert lies before us, the last barrier before Cathay. The sand is shot through with green, and the wind raises it in glowing veils that whisper as they pass. The wards I bought hum on every wagon. Where the dust touches them it falls away like ash from a fire. The guides say a caravan without them would be dead or mad in a week.

The Warpstone Desert lies before us, the last barrier before Cathay. The sand is shot through with green, and the wind raises it in glowing veils that whisper as they pass. Already two of the drivers have bleeding gums and one swears he hears his dead mother in the wind. We have no wards. An old man at the last oasis offers to guide us along the paths where the dust is thinnest, for a price. Or we could go round, by the long way, and lose half a year.
The wards hold.
The caravan crosses the Warpstone Desert unharmed.
Push on as fast as we can.
Pay the old man to guide us.
We take the long way round.
The journey will take half a year longer.
You come through unharmed.

In the high passes of the Mountains of Mourn the Ogres were waiting for us, as the caravan masters said they would be: a dozen of them, each the size of a wagon, with a Gnoblar on a pole for a banner. Their leader sniffs the tithe-token I carry, grunts and turns his back. For three weeks they walk with us, eat a goat each every night and kill anything that comes near. It is the safest I have felt since I left home.

In the high passes of the Mountains of Mourn the Ogres were waiting for us: a dozen of them, each the size of a wagon, with a Gnoblar on a pole for a banner. Their leader, a Bull with a cauldron strapped to his back, lays a hand on the lead ox and names the tithe. It is twice what the caravan masters said it would be. 'Pay ahead, pay less', he says, grinning with teeth like tombstones. 'Pay now, pay more. Or don't pay, and we eat.'
Walk with the escort.
The Ogres take the caravan safely through the Mountains of Mourn.
Pay the double tithe.
A feast first, then we will talk.
The Ogres eat, drink, laugh, and let you through for what you fed them.
The Ogres eat everything, then ask for the tithe anyway.
We fight our way through!
The Ogres respect strength. They let you through, and the tale of it will be told.
This is madness. We turn for home.

The Dark Lands. The sky is the colour of a bruise, the ground shakes at night, and rivers of fire run between black hills. Twice we have seen columns of slaves in chains on the horizon, driven east by bull-centaurs towards the smoking ziggurats of the Chaos Dwarfs, and the hobgoblin wolf riders who shadow the caravan by day are waiting for one of us to fall behind. The ash is in our food, our water and our lungs.
We travel by night along the old roads.
Hire hobgoblin guides.
For once, a hobgoblin keeps his word.
The word of a hobgoblin is worth what it always was. The guides lead you into a slavers' ambush, and you barely fight your way out.
March hard and keep the escort close.
An earthquake swallows two wagons and their loads.
Slavers fall on the rear of the caravan in the dark.

Three weeks out from port the sky turned green and the junk's captain ordered every sail down. Now the typhoon is on us: waves like mountains, the deck awash, and the ships of the Sea Dragon's fleet scattered out of sight. The captain lashes himself to the steering oar and laughs. The sailors burn paper offerings to Yin-Yin, the Sea Dragon, and pray.
Trust the captain.
Pray to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].

Off the coast of the Southlands black sails came over the horizon at dawn: a raiding fleet, Druchii corsairs or worse, and they are closing fast. The war junks of the Sea Dragon's fleet are turning to meet them, rockets on their decks, but there are only three of them. The captain asks what I want him to do.
Trust the war junks.
Fire-rockets set the corsairs' sails alight and they turn away.
The corsairs board the ship before the junks can drive them off.
Pay them to go away.
To arms! We fight on deck.
You lead the defence of the deck and throw the boarders into the sea.
The corsairs take you below in chains, and you are never seen again.

We have done it. The Dark Lands, the Mountains of Mourn, the Warpstone Desert: we came through them all, fewer than we set out and older than our years, and now we come down out of the hills into the [offmap_cathay.GetFullName], past the iron foundries of Shang-Yang, the city of Zhao Ming the Iron Dragon. The officials at the gate bow to us. Few westerners come this way alive, they say, and the Jade Dragon will hear of it.

After months at sea the junk sails into the harbour of Fu-Chow, the city of Yin-Yin the Sea Dragon, where a thousand ships ride at anchor under red sails. From there river barges carry us up into the heart of the [offmap_cathay.GetFullName]. Jade-roofed towns line the river, sky lanterns drift over the rice terraces at dusk, and everywhere the banners of the Celestial Dragon snap in the wind. There is so much to see before the Jade Dragon receives me.
This might reflect §Gwell§! on you, in the eyes of the Jade Dragon.
This character has travelled to Grand Cathay to kowtow before the Celestial Throne. The Jade Dragon, who keeps the court while the Dragon Emperor is away, was not impressed...
This character has travelled to Grand Cathay to kowtow before the Celestial Throne, and the Jade Dragon, who keeps the court while the Dragon Emperor is away, was pleased.
This character has travelled to Grand Cathay to kowtow before the Celestial Throne, and the Jade Dragon, who keeps the court while the Dragon Emperor is away, blessed them with his own hand!
This might reflect §Rpoorly§! on you, in the eyes of the Jade Dragon.
Kowtow Before the Celestial Throne

Journey to Wei-Jin in the §Y[offmap_cathay.GetFullName]§! and bow before the Celestial Throne, where Yuan Bo the Jade Dragon keeps the court while the Dragon Emperor is away. The road east is one of the most dangerous in the world: the Dark Lands, the Mountains of Mourn and the Warpstone Desert, or months at sea. Prepare well. Performing a Kowtow will earn you §GGrace§! with the §Y[offmap_cathay.GetFullName]§!, but it will cost you §RPrestige§! to do so.
